note: Hand-authored relationships over vendored sources. The one-way rule reference graph says an exception names the rule it overrides or extends; a base rule names nothing. A rules modification likewise names the base record whose meaning it changes, while its text and provenance remain in the vendored Hall of Heroes index. Generated indexes under datasets/rules-reference/ and datasets/rules-packs/ are rebuilt from PDFs on every harvest and deliberately carry no relationship fields, so authored relationships live here and only here. Each relationship records why, because a plausible-but-wrong relationship is the failure mode this corpus exists to eliminate. Reverse lookup is computed at query time by tools/Marvel.Rules.Index and never stored. See docs/rules-provenance.md.

ruling:121d5b7b5dcec377.why: Reveal says an attachment without attach-to text waits out of play, but does not say when it attaches. This ruling supplies the missing timing: its When Revealed ability creates and resolves the attachment target.

ruling:1bf319f7418a86d7.why: The FAQ ruling establishes that damage moved to a character counts as dealt damage. Rules Reference 1.8 states that clarification verbatim in Move clause 5, so the ruling remains citable but is absorbed.

ruling:6cb0530e539c7915.why: Cost clause 4 permits generating resources beyond a cost. This ruling resolves conflicting earlier guidance by establishing that overpaid resources are still spent for abilities that care about spending, while remaining not paid for that cost.

ruling:1516351f87fc4382.why: The RoRS persistent-damage rule records at most printed starting hit points. This correction clarifies that the next game still grants the Condition upgrade hit-point increase when it enters play; restoring the recorded dial must not erase that increase. RR 1.8 hit-points.2.3 retains the increase when a gets +X hit points ability takes effect.

ruling:420bd5b1763b9506.why: The February 2026 clarification applies resolve to both Widowmaker and Synth-Suit. RR 1.8 resolve requires at least one applied effect and excludes constant abilities and fully canceled abilities; the earlier trigger-based stunned Attacrobatics answer does not govern this updated wording.

ruling:6e301a347a5392fb.why: The July 2023 answer explicitly updates the conflicting earlier Defender rulings: a discarded minion must actually engage before threat or Confused can be removed. Emptying the deck completes only the discard instruction, not the subsequent entry cost.

ruling:a1f4982cfebcd768.why: The April 2026 clarification places effect initiation after arrow costs; an acquired status or Patrol can prevent that effect. This supersedes the older Defender and Baron Zemo answer that treated the thwart as already initiated.

ruling:6d6264d6620980b3.why: The February 2026 ruling explicitly declares the older Marked for Death ruling outdated: only the identity-specific Mockingbird is tucked out of play, and only that tucked copy returns to its owner's hand. It does not create a general exception for other faceup attachments.

ruling:b216c9af67e04d26.why: Quiver's top-five search shuffles the entire deck after completion. This applies the current search rule to Quiver rather than replacing the general rule.

ruling:3bdad6b3608ce352.why: Quiver may search a nonempty deck even if the player knows no Arrow is in its top five; search is exempt from the ordinary known-valid-target initiation requirement. The exhaust cost and nonempty search area still apply.

rr:acceleration-icon.why: Step one places the main scheme's printed acceleration threat. Each acceleration icon in play adds one more.

rr:assault.why: A basic thwart removes threat equal to the character's THW. Assault substitutes ATK for THW against a scheme carrying the keyword.

rr:confuse-confused.why: A character may use its basic thwart power. A confused status card cancels the next thwart and removes itself instead.

rr:crisis-icon.why: Threat is removed from a scheme by thwarting and by card effects. A crisis icon in play forbids player cards from removing it from the main scheme.

rr:guard.why: Base rules let a hero or ally attack any enemy that can be attacked. Guard removes the villain from that set while the guarding minion is engaged.

rr:hinder-x.why: Threat is placed on schemes. Hinder X puts X threat on the card carrying the keyword as it enters play.

rr:incite-x.why: Threat arrives on the main scheme from scheming and from card effects. Incite X places X of it when the card is revealed.

rr:overkill.why: Base damage application places damage on the character it was dealt to and nothing transfers. Overkill adds a transfer of the excess to the villain or the controlling identity.

rr:patrol.why: A character may use its basic thwart power against a scheme. Patrol forbids the engaged player using cards they control to thwart the main scheme.

rr:peril.why: Players may normally consult and act freely during another player's resolution. Peril forbids the consultation and forbids other players playing cards or triggering abilities while it resolves.

rr:permanent.why: A card in play can be defeated or otherwise leave play. Permanent forbids it except to abilities in the same set.

rr:piercing.why: Tough prevents damage. Piercing discards tough status cards from the attacked character before damage is dealt, so it removes the prevention rather than the damage.

rr:quickstrike.why: Minions activate during step two of the villain phase. Quickstrike makes a minion attack on engaging, outside that step.

rr:ranged.why: Retaliate deals damage back to an attacker. Ranged makes an attack ignore it.

rr:requirement-resources.why: A resource cost may normally be paid with any mix of types. Requirement forbids playing the card unless the specified resources are among those spent.

rr:retaliate-x.why: An enemy attack resolves against the defender. Retaliate adds damage back to the attacker after it does.

rr:stalwart.why: Status cards may be given to a character. Stalwart forbids the confused and stunned ones outright.

rr:steady.why: A character cannot hold more than one status card of each type. Steady raises that limit by one for confused and for stunned.

rr:stun-stunned.why: A character may use its basic attack power. A stunned status card cancels the next such attack and removes itself instead.

rr:surge.why: Step four reveals the cards a player was dealt. Surge adds another card to that process when the card carrying it is revealed.

rr:teamwork.why: Minions activate during step two of the villain phase. Teamwork makes a minion activate on entering play, outside that step.

rr:temporary.why: A card in play remains until something removes it. Temporary forces its discard at the end of the round.

rr:tough.why: A tough status card cancels the damage a character would take, which is an exception to base damage application.

rr:toughness.why: Tough is a status a character can be given. Toughness gives it automatically on entering play.

rr:uses-x-type.why: All-purpose counters are a shared token pool. Uses X places X of them on the card as it enters play, as its own supply.

rr:victory-x.why: A card leaving play goes to a discard pile or out of the game. Victory X sends it to the victory display instead, worth X.

rr:villainous.why: A basic power is used at its printed value. Villainous gives the character a boost card whose icons modify that value for the activation.
